learning: If slalom line loss stays at 0.1 or below, the inertia lever is not yet exhausted and the controller can stay fixed. If line loss reaches 0.2 or more, inertia is the cause and it should not be reduced further. max_error at about 0.062 m has stayed the same across every geometry and gain tried, so progress and line loss are the signals to track.
notes: Midpoint inertia test on the iteration-9 reference controller. Only mass (0.8 to 0.75) and body_length (0.18 to 0.16) change from the reproduced 111.80 platform. Slalom line loss is the stop signal: at 0.2 or above, revert to the baseline inertia.
rationale: Iteration 9 reproduced the iteration-5 platform (wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, sensors at y 0.03 with a 0.06 m span, 16 mm footprints) and scored 111.80, with slalom line loss 0.10. That confirms the platform and the controller (kp 3.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, last_direction) as the reference. Iteration 4 showed that lower inertia (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) gave the best progress (oval 0.53, s-bend 0.20, score 124.20) but slalom line loss of 0.85. Iterations 6 to 8 showed that wheel_track 0.10 cost progress and line retention at every kp tried. The Builder's iteration-10 geometry is the midpoint inertia test I recommended: mass 0.75 and body_length 0.16, with everything else unchanged. Yaw inertia m(L²+W²)/12 is about 0.00250 at the midpoint, between 0.00312 at the baseline and 0.00198 at iteration 4. I expect some of the progress gain to return while slalom line loss stays under the 0.2 stop rule. The controller stays exactly as the iteration-9 reference, so this race isolates inertia. I am not retuning gains, because every gain change so far was confounded with a geometry change or raised line loss. Expected result, not measured: slalom line loss between 0.1 and 0.2, oval progress above 0.55, and a score near 112 to 125.
